scope: Bounded read-only review; reviewer did not execute the new checked candidate or mutate compiler/runtime sources. Actual candidate gates remain separate.
verdict: No blocking defect found in the reviewed source changes; promotion remains contingent on checked candidate controls and full relevant gates.

findings.assessment: driver_emit_owned executes after checked completion but before JS reachability pruning, native generation or library emission. Check-only and pure interpreter paths return earlier. Existing OWNED-name diagnostics retain priority; only an empty reserved-name result reaches the foreign/constructor scan.

findings.area: Exact foreign/constructor identity and first error
findings.assessment: Scan preserves the current full-book definition order, tests only Def entries with annotation-stripped Foreign bodies, and resolves exact qualified constructor names through the existing j_find_ctor. Base provenance does not exempt a collision, matching upstream def_foreign/book_owned. The first matching foreign definition wins; qualified/case-distinct names remain separate.

nc_ctor_codes emits the decimal value of each character with an underscore delimiter. The resulting sequence preserves source character boundaries, case and punctuation; empty name also has a distinct representation. Prefix FID_ makes valid C identifiers. Numeric/underscore encoded suffixes cannot equal fixed alphabetic runtime FIDs.

Segment definitions, closure/task references, continuations, dispatch, arity validation and foreign symbolic FID(name) all pass through nt_fid. MAIN_FID now uses nt_fid(main). Numeric segment ordering and arity/result tables do not change. Runtime FID_IO_EMIT/FID_EXIT/FID_ENTER and BEND_CLO_APPLY remain fixed.

nc_foreign_parts resolves FID names via existing nc_ref_name then applies the new nt_fid, including native-wrapper names. Constructor IDs and scoped CID aliasing are unchanged. Bounded scan found no literal source-function FID token dependency in maintained runtime/effect C; uppercase FID spellings in pinned Bend tests are explanatory comments. Raw private generated identifier spellings are not asserted as an external stable ABI.

Direct ownership fixture covers reserved-name priority, two colliding foreign definitions in deliberate order, unused scope behavior via execution controls, exact qualified/case distinctions and Base foreign collision. Source controls include dotted/underscored/case variants, reserved-looking function names and actual C FID(a.b)/FID(a_b) translation. These are reviewed test intentions, not reviewer-acquired pass results.

tradeoffs: Encoded names are longer and can increase emitted C bytes, compiler input parsing and diagnostics size; no generated-program speedup or unchanged Clang compile cost follows.
Foreign-name validation scans the whole book and reuses a linear constructor lookup for each foreign definition. This is emission-stage work only; check-only ordinary performance bypasses it.
Static reasoning is not proof of every loader ordering or external foreign-program contract; checked multi-error/import/foreign execution controls remain the validation boundary.
